question: For the patients whose total cholesterol is higher than normal, how many of them have a negative measure of degree of coagulation?
evidence: total cholesterol is higher than normal refers to `T-CHO` > = 250; negative measure of degree of coagulation refers to KCT = '-' ;
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Examination AS T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE T2."T-CHO" >= 250 AND T3.KCT = '-'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Examination AS T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE T2.`T-CHO` >= 250 AND T3.KCT = '-'

b.request: Count the distinct patient IDs with at least one Laboratory record where `T-CHO` >= 250 and at least one Examination record where `KCT` = '-'
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.ID) FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 250 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination AS e WHERE e.ID = l.ID AND e.KCT = '-')

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.ID) FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Examination AS e ON e.ID = l.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 250 AND e.KCT = '-';

d.request: How many distinct patient IDs have T-CHO ≥ 250 and KCT = '-'?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.ID) FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Examination AS e ON l.ID = e.ID WHERE l.`T-CHO` >= 250 AND e.KCT = '-';
